title: improv·artist · systematic (Sol LeWitt)
mutation_directive: improv artist: systematic via Sol LeWitt

improv_extras.practice: rule-based wall drawings; the instruction IS the art; combinatorial

v1.feedback: The LeWitt concept lands — combinatorial grid cells with rule-assigned line directions is faithful to his wall-drawing instructions, and the sequential reveal is a nice touch. But the piece reads as a flat 2D grid of hatched squares; the z-extrusion is too subtle to register, so it looks like a texture swatch rather than a spatial installation. Push the depth scale so diagonal cells visibly lift off the wall plane, or rotate the camera ~15° off-axis so parallax sells the relief. The graphite-on-white palette is correctly restrained but the four tint variants are nearly indistinguishable — widen the hue gaps just enough that a viewer can decode which rule each cell executes without squinting, which is core to LeWitt's combinatorial legibility.

v2.feedback: The combinatorial grid logic and serpentine reveal genuinely channel LeWitt's instruction-based practice, and the four-hue palette on warm white reads immediately as a wall drawing. However, the particles are essentially dot-stippled straight lines — the piece doesn't leverage the particle medium beyond what a 2D canvas stroke could do. A refined version should let the rule-following process itself become visible motion: animate particles tracing their assigned directions in real time (like a draftsperson executing the instruction), or let neighboring cells' line fields interfere at boundaries to produce emergent moiré or weave patterns that reward sustained viewing. The depth extrusion per rule is too subtle at default camera — either commit to a more sculptural z-separation with clear parallax on orbit, or flatten it and own the wall-drawing flatness fully.
